messages:
alex_support: Hey SRE team, multiple customers reporting bursts of 429s + elevated latencies starting ~2025-02-10T14:07:14Z. They say their steady streams get a few seconds of full success then a wall of 429s.

ci-bot: deploy finished: limiter-config v3.0.0 -> prod @ 2025-02-10T14:05:00Z

kevin_infra: I see the config change in the Helm values: "burst_tokens: 0" - that was supposed to default to 50. The templating rule that merges env overrides clobbered the default.

alex_support: Customer logs (redacted):
```
2025-02-10T14:07:12Z POST /v1/chat 200 110ms
2025-02-10T14:07:13Z POST /v1/chat 429 6ms
2025-02-10T14:07:13Z POST /v1/chat 429 5ms
2025-02-10T14:07:15Z POST /v1/chat 200 120ms
2025-02-10T14:07:16Z POST /v1/chat 429 4ms
```
Looks like short windows of acceptance then rejects.

rahul_prodeng: With burst_tokens at 0, the token bucket has no leaky buffer -> any alignment in refill produces tight acceptance windows. If many frontends request at similar times, we get oscillation.

tanya_oncall: Can we hotfix to set burst_tokens back to 50 and patch templating? This is customer-impacting.

kevin_infra: Initiating emergency patch now. Applying patch to helm values to restore burst_tokens: 50 and rolling limiter pods in region-us-east-1. Doing canary first.

ci-bot: rollout started: limiter-service config-rollout -> 2/4 pods updated

nina_prodeng: Also note metrics: per-tenant queue length and per-node "accepted_fraction" show sawtooth pattern from 14:06:45 -> 14:09:30. Strong correlation to config rollout at 14:05.

mike_sre: After canary finishes, I'm going to add a temporary countermeasure: enable per-tenant smoothing (server-side short-term grace) so sudden zero-burst won't immediately drop to 0 throughput.

ci-bot: rollout completed: limiter-service config-rollout -> success @ 2025-02-10T14:11:30Z

alex_support: Customer confirms errors dropped ~14:11:50 after fix; they appreciate the quick rollback. They asked for a clear explanation and for SDK best-practices.

rahul_prodeng: Root cause draft: release v3.0.0 included a Helm values overlay that unintentionally set burst_tokens to 0 for all limiter instances. Without buffer tokens, traffic with small oscillations caused synchronized acceptance windows and transient mass throttling. Remediation: restore sane default, add unit test for values merge, add randomized refill jitter, and add a pre-deploy validation that checks for suspicious limits (burst_tokens >= 10).

kevin_infra: Action items:
- (Kevin) Fix templating merge + add unit tests — due 48h
- (Mike) Implement per-tenant smoothing toggle + tests — due 72h
- (Nina) Dashboard: add "burst_buffer_size" and alert if <10 in prod — due 24h
- (Tanya) Draft customer note and KB entry on burst 429s + SDK jitter/backoff examples — due 24h

rahul_prodeng: Also: update 429 payload to include "throttle_type": "burst" or "quota" and include a short hint for recovery. Example:
```
{"error":"rate_limit","throttle_type":"burst","retry_after_ms":400,"node_hint":"lim-us-east-1-03"}
```

alex_support: I'll coordinate the ACME follow-up tomorrow and offer temporary credits if their SLA was impacted.

tanya_oncall: Incident window: 14:06:40 - 14:12:00 UTC. No user data lost. Marking P1 -> mitigated; will move to postmortem.

mike_sre: Adding a replayable test to the chaos suite to exercise zero-burst config and ensure throttling pattern doesn't recur.

kevin_infra: Rolling change to CI: validation job will fail if any production Helm overlay sets critical numeric limits to zero unless explicitly allowed.

alex_support: Thanks team. Customer is asking if we can proactively notify when config changes touch limiter defaults. Can we add a config-change subscription in the console?

rahul_prodeng: Good idea. Adding to roadmap: config-change notifications + a dedicated audit log for limiter parameter changes.

tanya_oncall: Closing notes: please attach logs and graphs to INC-2025-4001 and tag eng-runtime + infra. :thumbsup:
